AuthDetailQuery.description:
The query of endpoint 22: which key the screen sent (COPAUS1C-003).

- `direction` absent: ENTER, a first entry from COPAUS0C's selection, or a refresh. The
  authorization the path names is read and shown (COPAUS1C-008).
- `direction=forward`: F8, `PROCESS-PF8-KEY`. The authorization after the one the path names
  is shown, or the same one with `Already at the last Authorization...` (COPAUS1C-024,
  COPAUS1C-025).

`backward` is no key of this screen. It deserialises, so the request is not rejected here,
and the service answers it as the `WHEN OTHER` branch of `EVALUATE EIBAID` does, with ENTER's
processing. The query takes no `page_size`: the endpoint addresses one authorization, not a
collection (Bounded Pagination).

oneOf.description: `forward` for F8, the next authorization; absent for ENTER.

AuthDetailResponse.description:
One authorization as COPAUS1C's `POPULATE-AUTH-DETAILS` fills `COPAU1A`, the key the screen
keeps for it, and the message row (COPAUS1C-012 to COPAUS1C-025, COPAUS1C-034, COPAUS1C-035).

Each text member holds exactly its map field's width in characters, trailing spaces
included, except a masked member whose redacted SSN needs more room than its trailing spaces
give: it is longer by the difference, as an SSN that fills the 9 bytes of the ZIP shows as
its 11-character redacted form, one more than `MERZIP` ([`redact_free_text`]). It has no
`Deserialize`: the card number it carries is redacted.

acct_id.description:
The account, `CDEMO-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11)`: its 11 digits with the leading zeros. The screen
keeps it for the next request (COPAUS1C-003).

amount.description:
Amount, `AUTHAMT` (12): the approved amount edited by `-zzzzzzz9.99`, as the domain
renders it (COPAUS1C-015).

auth_code.description: Auth Code, `AUTHCD` (6): the processing code's six digits (COPAUS1C-019).

auth_date.description:
Auth Date, `AUTHDT` (10): `MM/DD/YY` from the stored `YYMMDD`, then two spaces
(COPAUS1C-013).

auth_key.description:
The shown authorization's key, `PA-AUTHORIZATION-KEY`, as the 16-digit `{auth_key}` path
segment of endpoints 22 and 23. After F8 it is the next authorization's key, which the
screen keeps; after ENTER, F5 and F8 at the last authorization it is unchanged
(COPAUS1C-003, COPAUS1C-024, COPAUS1C-025, COPAUS1C-034).

auth_time.description:
Auth Time, `AUTHTM` (10): `HH:MM:SS` from the stored `HHMMSS`, then two spaces
(COPAUS1C-014).

auth_type.description:
Auth Type, `AUTHTYP` (14): `PA-AUTH-TYPE`, then ten spaces, masked as the transaction ID
is (COPAUS1C-021, E32).

card_expiry.description:
Card Exp. Date, `CRDEXP` (5): `MM/YY` text built from the four stored bytes of
`PA-CARD-EXPIRY-DATE PIC X(04)`, not a date (COPAUS1C-020).

card_num.description:
Card #, `CARDNUM` (16): twelve `*` and the card's last four digits, never the full
number (COPAUS1C-012, COPAU01-013, E32).

fraud_status.description:
Fraud Status, `AUTHFRD` (10): `F` or `R`, `-` and the report date, or `-` and nine
spaces when the authorization was never reported (COPAUS1C-022).

match_status.description:
Match Status, `AUTHMTC` (1): the stored byte, masked as the transaction ID is
(COPAUS1C-021, E32).

merchant_category_code.description:
MCC Code, `MCCCD` (4): `PA-MERCHANT-CATAGORY-CODE`, masked as the source is
(COPAUS1C-020, E32).

merchant_city.description:
City, `MERCITY` (25): `PA-MERCHANT-CITY`, then twelve spaces, masked as the name is
(COPAUS1C-023, E32).

merchant_id.description: Merchant ID, `MERID` (15): `PA-MERCHANT-ID`, masked as the name is (COPAUS1C-023, E32).

merchant_name.description:
Name, `MERNAME` (25): `PA-MERCHANT-NAME`, then three spaces, masked by
[`redact_free_text`] as stored request text, so a card number or an SSN in the name shows
only in its redacted form (COPAUS1C-023, E32).

merchant_state.description: State, `MERST` (2): `PA-MERCHANT-STATE`, masked as the name is (COPAUS1C-023, E32).

merchant_zip.description:
Zip, `MERZIP` (10): `PA-MERCHANT-ZIP`, then one space, masked as the name is. An SSN
that fills the 9 bytes shows as its 11-character redacted form, one character more than
the map field (COPAUS1C-023, E32).

message.description:
The message row, `ERRMSG` (78): none after ENTER or a found F8 (COPAUS1C-035),
`Already at the last Authorization...` after F8 at the account's last authorization
(COPAUS1C-025), `AUTH MARKED FRAUD...` or `AUTH FRAUD REMOVED...` after a committed F5
(COPAUS1C-032).

pos_entry_mode.description: POS Entry Mode, `POSEMD` (4): the two digits, then two spaces (COPAUS1C-020).

reason.description:
Resp Reason, `AUTHRSN` (20): the reason code, `-` and its description, or
`9999-ERROR` for a code outside the table (COPAUS1C-017, COPAUS1C-018).

response.description: Auth Resp, `AUTHRSP` (1): `A` for response code `00`, `D` otherwise (COPAUS1C-016).

source.description:
Source, `AUTHSRC` (10): `PA-MESSAGE-SOURCE`, then four spaces, masked by
[`redact_free_text`] as stored request text (COPAUS1C-020, E32).

transaction_id.description:
Tran Id, `TRNID` (15): `PA-TRANSACTION-ID`, masked by [`redact_free_text`] as stored
request text: an SSN in it shows as `***-**-` and its last four digits, and the 12-digit
run of `TXN000000000001` as `TXN********0001` (COPAUS1C-021, E32).

AuthSummaryBlock.description:
The customer and summary block of `COPAU0A`, every value as its map field shows it, padding
included (COPAUS0C-020 to COPAUS0C-025, COPAUS0C-027 to COPAUS0C-029).

The map's one-byte `Acct Status` field has no member: COPAUS0C never fills it, so it is
always blank and endpoint 21 returns no account status (COPAUS0C-026).

address_line_1.description: The first address row, `ADDR001` (25): address lines 1 and 2 (COPAUS0C-022).

address_line_2.description: The second address row, `ADDR002` (25): address line 3, state and ZIP (COPAUS0C-023).

approved_amount.description: Appr Amt, `APPRAMT` (10): through `-zzzz9.99` and one space (COPAUS0C-028).

approved_count.description: Approval #, `APPRCNT` (3): the approved count as 3 digits (COPAUS0C-028).

cash_limit.description:
Cash Lim, `CASHLIM` (9): the account's cash credit limit through `-zzzz9.99`
(COPAUS0C-025).

credit_limit.description:
Credit Lim, `CREDLIM` (12): the account's credit limit through `-zzzzzzz9.99`
(COPAUS0C-025).

customer_id.description:
Customer Id, `CUSTID` (9): the customer's 9 digits with their leading zeros
(COPAUS0C-020).

customer_name.description: Name, `CNAME` (25): first name, middle initial and last name (COPAUS0C-021).

declined_amount.description: Decl Amt, `DECLAMT` (10): through `-zzzz9.99` and one space (COPAUS0C-028).

declined_count.description: Decline #, `DECLCNT` (3): the declined count as 3 digits (COPAUS0C-028).

phone.description: PH, `PHONE1` (13): the first 13 characters of phone 1 (COPAUS0C-024).

summary_found.description:
Whether the account has a pending-authorization summary. Without one the six figures
below are `0` characters filling each field and the list is empty, a normal outcome
(COPAUS0C-028, COPAUS0C-029).

AuthSummaryQuery.description:
The query of endpoint 21: absent members are ENTER or a first entry, which shows the first
page; `direction` with a `page_key` is F8 or F7 (COPAUS0C-008, COPAUS0C-041, COPAUS0C-047).

oneOf.description:
`forward` (F8) pages after `page_key`, `backward` (F7) from it; absent with a `page_key`
pages forward, and without one the first page is shown whatever the direction.

page_key.description:
F8: the `last_key` of the page shown; F7: the `first_key` the screen saved for the page
before it. The 16 digits of an authorization key exactly as a response renders them; any
other text is rejected with 400 on field `page_key`.

page_size.description:
Rows per page, 1 to 100; absent, the 5 rows of the map. A value outside that range is
rejected with 422 (Bounded Pagination). The screen never sends it.

AuthSummaryResponse.description:
The 200 of endpoint 21: the account, its block and one page of its pending authorizations,
with the keys and the next-page flag the screen keeps in its paging state (COPAUS0C-008,
COPAUS0C-031, COPAUS0C-036, COPAUS0C-039). A successful read carries no message
(COPAUS0C-052).

acct_id.description: The account read, 11 digits with their leading zeros, which the account field shows.

first_key.description:
The first row's `auth_key`, which the screen saves as this page's first key for F7;
`null` with no rows (COPAUS0C-039).

has_next_page.description:
The next-page flag after a full page: `true` when another authorization follows it,
`false` when none does. `null` when the page holds fewer than `page_size` rows: the
program leaves the flag unset, and the screen keeps the value an earlier page gave it
(COPAUS0C-036).

last_key.description:
The last row's `auth_key`, the `page_key` of the next F8; `null` with no rows
(COPAUS0C-039).

rows.description:
Up to `page_size` rows in key order; empty without a summary, or when no detail has the
requested `page_key` (COPAUS0C-029, COPAUS0C-041, COPAUS0C-047).

summary.description:
The customer and summary block, returned whether or not a summary exists
(COPAUS0C-028, COPAUS0C-029).

AuthSummaryRow.description:
One row of the list, as `POPULATE-AUTH-LIST` fills it, and the key that selects it
(COPAUS0C-032 to COPAUS0C-034). It holds no card number (COPAUS0C-055).

`date` and `time` are the display strings the program builds, not typed values: they come
from `PA-AUTH-ORIG-DATE` and `PA-AUTH-ORIG-TIME`, `PIC X(06)` fields outside the `X(10)` dates
and `X(26)` timestamps that Typed Dates and Timestamps covers, copied with no calendar check,
so a stored `241399` shows `13/99/24`, which no date type holds (COPAUS0C-034).

auth_key.description:
The row's authorization key as 16 digits: the `{auth_key}` path segment of endpoints 22
and 23 for an `S` on this row, and the `page_key` of the next F7 or F8 when it is the
page's first or last row (COPAUS0C-010, COPAUS0C-034).

auth_type.description:
Type, `PTYPEnn` (4): the stored authorization type, masked as the transaction ID is; its
4 bytes hold no written number of nine digits and show as stored (COPAUS0C-032, E32).

match_status.description:
STS, `PSTATnn` (1): the stored match status, masked as the transaction ID is; its one
byte shows as stored (COPAUS0C-032, E32).

transaction_id.description:
Transaction ID, `TRNIDnn` (16): the 15 stored characters and one space, masked by
[`redact_free_text`] as stored request text, as endpoint 22 masks it: `TX0000000000001`
shows as `TX*********0001`, a 9-digit SSN as `***-**-` and its last four digits, and a
run of fewer than nine digits as stored. A Tran Id whose SSN fills its last nine bytes is
one character longer than the 16 of the map field: the redacted form adds two, the one
trailing space gives back one (COPAUS0C-032, COPAUS1C-021, E32).

BillPaymentRequest.description:
The two inputs of `COBIL0A`, each the raw text of its map field.

Only the map `LENGTH` is checked here, the server half of the `both` rows `COBIL00-013` and
`COBIL00-020` of `modern/audit/screens.md`. An absent member is the empty text, which the
program's own edit answers with `Acct ID can NOT be empty...` (COBIL00C-007). The values are
neither trimmed nor upper-cased: COBIL00C reads them as typed.

acct_id.description:
`ACTIDIN`, the account ID, at most 11 characters (`COBIL00-013`). Eleven digits name an
account; a blank value is refused (COBIL00C-007, COBIL00C-008).

confirm.description:
`CONFIRM`, at most 1 character (`COBIL00-020`): blank shows the balance, `Y` or `y` pays,
`N` or `n` clears; any other value is refused (COBIL00C-009 to COBIL00C-012).

BillPaymentResult.description:
The screen a 200 of endpoint 15 shows: the account, the balance, the message row and the new
transaction ID.

`cleared` is true where the program ran `INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS` before its last send: after
`N` (COBIL00C-010) and after a written payment (COBIL00C-028). The screen then empties its
inputs and its balance, and shows `message`.

acct_id.description:
`ACTIDIN` as shown: the 11 digits of the account whose balance is shown, and the empty
text where the screen is cleared (COBIL00C-010, COBIL00C-019, COBIL00C-028).

cleared.description:
Whether the screen empties its inputs and balance: after `N` (COBIL00C-010) and after a
payment (COBIL00C-028).

current_balance.description:
`CURBAL`, the balance as `PIC +9999999999.99` edits it, 14 characters such as
`+0000000843.00`; present only with the confirmation prompt (COBIL00C-017, COBIL00C-019,
ARITH-019).

message.description:
The message row: `Confirm to make a bill payment...` with the balance (COBIL00C-019),
`Payment successful.  Your Transaction ID is <id>.` after a payment (COBIL00C-028), absent
after `N` (COBIL00C-010).

new_tran_id.description:
`TRAN-ID` of the payment just written, 16 digits; present only after a payment
(COBIL00C-023, COBIL00C-028).

example.message: Confirm to make a bill payment...

CardListQuery.description:
The query of endpoint 7: the two filters as typed, the key pressed, and the paging state of
the previous response, echoed unchanged.

Every member is optional. A request with none of them is the fresh start of the list
(COCRDLIC-002, COCRDLIC-017): page 1 from the lowest card number, with no filter.

card_num.description:
`CARDSID`, the card filter, as typed (map `LENGTH` 16). Blank, or sixteen `0` digits, is
no filter (COCRDLIC-007); sixteen digits list only that card (COCRDLIC-010); anything else
is 400 with field `card_num` (COCRDLIC-008). Input only: never sent back.

oneOf.description:
The key pressed: `forward` for F8, `backward` for F7, absent for ENTER or any key the
program processes as ENTER (COCRDLIC-003).

first_key.description:
The `first_key` of the previous response: the `card_ref` that ENTER and F7 read from
(COCRDLIC-018, COCRDLIC-026, COCRDLIC-027). Absent, the browse starts below every card.

has_next_page.description:
The `has_next_page` of the previous response. Absent, no next page: F8 then re-reads the
page from `first_key` (COCRDLIC-024).

last_key.description:
The `last_key` of the previous response: the `card_ref` that F8 reads from while a next
page exists (COCRDLIC-023).

last_page_shown.description:
The `last_page_shown` of the previous response: whether F8 already showed the last page,
so that a further F8 answers `NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY` (COCRDLIC-024, COCRDLIC-025).
Absent, not shown.

page_no.description:
The page number of the previous response, 0 to 9 (`PAGENO`, COCRDLIC-030). Absent, page 1.
Outside 0 to 9 it is 400 with field `page_no`.

page_size.description:
Rows per page, 1 to 100 (Bounded Pagination); any other value is 422. Absent, 7, the
program's screen size. The screen never sends it.

reread.description:
`true` for the re-read after a selection error the screen found (COCRDLIC-014): the list
is read again from the start of the card file under the filters, the echoed page number
is kept and the key pressed still decides the messages. Absent, an ordinary request.

CardListResponse.description:
One page of the card list: what COCRDLIC's `1000-SEND-MAP` shows after a read, and the
paging state the next request echoes (COCRDLIC-017 to COCRDLIC-034).

Always a 200, the empty page of `NO RECORDS FOUND FOR THIS SEARCH CONDITION.` included
(COCRDLIC-021).

blank_rows_above.description:
The empty rows above the first listed card: 0, except after a backward read that reached
the start of the card file, whose cards fill the rows from the last one upward
(COCRDLIC-029).

first_key.description:
The `card_ref` of the page's first key, where ENTER and F7 read from; echoed as
`first_key`. `null` before any card was listed.

has_next_page.description: Whether F8 moves to a next page (COCRDLIC-019, COCRDLIC-020). Echoed as `has_next_page`.

info_message.description: `INFOMSG`: `TYPE S FOR DETAIL, U TO UPDATE ANY RECORD`, or `null` (COCRDLIC-033).

last_key.description:
The `card_ref` of the page's last key, where F8 reads from while a next page exists: the
card after the page when one exists (COCRDLIC-019). Echoed as `last_key`.

last_page_shown.description:
Whether F8 has shown the last page (COCRDLIC-024, COCRDLIC-025). Echoed as
`last_page_shown`.

message.description:
`ERRMSG`: the error line, such as `NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW` or
`NO PREVIOUS PAGES TO DISPLAY`, exactly as the program moves it (COCRDLIC-034); `null`
when the line is empty.

page_no.description: `PAGENO`: the page number, one digit, 0 to 9 (COCRDLIC-022, COCRDLIC-030).

rows.description: The listed cards in screen order, ascending by card number, at most the page size.

CardListRow.description:
One listed card (COCRDLIC-032): row `n` of the map, `ACCTNOn`, `CRDNUMn` and `CRDSTSn`
(`COCRDLI-030` to `COCRDLI-032` for row 1), with the card's handle.

No card verification code, embossed name or expiry date is listed.

acct_id.description: `ACCTNOn`: the card's account, `CARD-ACCT-ID`, as its eleven digits with leading zeros.

card_num.description:
`CRDNUMn`: the card number redacted to twelve `*` and its last four digits, 16
characters; the full number is never sent (`E32`).

card_ref.description:
The card's handle, the `cards.card_ref` identity, which a selection carries to
`/cards/view` or `/cards/update` and which endpoints 8 to 10 accept.

status.description:
`CRDSTSn`: `CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS`, the stored byte as one character, a space included
(COCRDLIC-032).

CardLookupQuery.description:
The query string of endpoint 8 (and of endpoint 9): the account and the card to show
(COCRDSLC-006 to COCRDSLC-013).

Every member is the raw text of its screen field. An absent `acct_id` is the empty text, which
COCRDSLC's edit answers with `'Account number not provided'` or `'No input received'`. The
card is named by `card_num`, the typed number, or by `card_ref`, the handle a COCRDLI list
row or an earlier response carries (COCRDSLC-026); the domain edit, not this DTO, decides
that exactly one of the two is supplied, so its messages stay the program's.

`Debug` masks `card_num` and `Serialize` omits it (Cardholder Data Redaction).

acct_id.description: `ACCTSID` (`ACCTSIDI PIC X(11)`): the account number, 11 digits (COCRDSL-013).

card_num.description:
`CARDSID` (`CARDSIDI PIC X(16)`): the card number as typed, 16 digits (COCRDSL-016).
Never sent together with `card_ref`.

card_ref.description:
The `cards.card_ref` handle of the card (CVACT02Y-008), from a COCRDLI list row or from
an earlier [`CardViewResponse`] (COCRDSLC-006, COCRDSLC-026). Never sent together with
`card_num`.

CardUpdateFields.description:
The raw text of the four enterable detail fields of an endpoint 10 request, at most the map
`LENGTH` of each (COCRDUP-019, COCRDUP-022, COCRDUP-025, COCRDUP-027).

An absent member is the empty text, which the program reads as blank (COCRDUPC-009). The
screen zero-fills a shorter month or year on the left before sending it (COCRDUPC-033). The
expiry day is no input: it is the snapshot's.

embossed_name.description: `CRDNAME` (`CRDNAMEI PIC X(50)`): the name on the card, edited by `1230-EDIT-NAME`.

expiry_month.description: `EXPMON` (`EXPMONI PIC X(2)`): the expiry month, edited by `1250-EDIT-EXPIRY-MON`.

expiry_year.description: `EXPYEAR` (`EXPYEARI PIC X(4)`): the expiry year, edited by `1260-EDIT-EXPIRY-YEAR`.

status.description:
`CRDSTCD` (`CRDSTCDI PIC X(1)`): the active status, `Y` or `N`, edited by
`1240-EDIT-CARDSTATUS`.

CardUpdateRequest.description:
The body of endpoint 10: the key, the raw text of the detail fields and the echoed snapshot,
whose `state` the last response set (COCRDUPC-044).

The handler passes it to the service owned; the service builds the domain's input with
[`CardUpdateFields::input`] and its snapshot through `From<&CardUpdateSnapshot>`.

fields.description: The raw text of the four detail fields.

snapshot.description: The snapshot of the fetch, with the state of the last response.

CardUpdateResult.description:
The 200 body of endpoint 10: the screen `3000-SEND-MAP` sends after a validation, a save or
a restart, none of which has an error message (COCRDUPC-034, COCRDUPC-035, COCRDUPC-039).

The fields keep the text the request sent. `snapshot` is what the client echoes next, already
in `state`; it is `null` after a restart, when the screen searches again through endpoint 9.

info_message.description:
`INFOMSGO` (40): the info line of the state the response leaves, `Changes validated.Press
F5 to save`, `Changes committed to database` or `Please enter Account and Card Number`
(COCRDUPC-034, COCRDUPC-039).

save_enabled.description: Whether `F5=Save F12=Cancel` is shown: with the confirmation prompt only (COCRDUPC-034).

oneOf.description: The snapshot to echo next; `null` after a restart.

state.description:
`CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION` after the response: `changes_ok_not_confirmed` after a validation,
`changes_okayed_and_done` after a save, `not_fetched` after a restart.

CardUpdateSnapshot.description:
`CCUP-OLD-DETAILS` and `CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION`: the values endpoint 9 fetched and the state the
last response left, which the client echoes in every endpoint 10 request (COCRDUPC-044).

It holds the account as entered, the name upper-cased, the typed expiry date with its day and
the status; the name and status keep every byte of their fields, trailing spaces included
(COCRDUPC-017). It holds no card number, because the card is the path's `card_ref`, and no
card verification code, which cannot leave the service (module docs). A value the client
alters equals no stored value, so it reads as a change and, at a save, as a card changed by
another user: the snapshot grants nothing (`X-COCRDUPC-1`).

acct_id.description:
`CCUP-OLD-ACCTID PIC X(11)`: the account entered for the search or the list row's, 11
digits, which a save writes into the card (COCRDUPC-038, `X-COCRDUPC-2`).

embossed_name.description:
`CCUP-OLD-CRDNAME PIC X(50)`: the stored name, upper-cased at the fetch, all 50 bytes
(COCRDUPC-017).

expiration_date.description:
`CCUP-OLD-EXPYEAR`, `CCUP-OLD-EXPMON` and `CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY`: the stored expiry date,
`null` when it is blank.

state.description: `CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION`: the state the last response left.

status.description: `CCUP-OLD-CRDSTCD PIC X(1)`: the stored active status.

CardUpdateState.description:
`CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION PIC X(1)` (`COCRDUPC.cbl:276-290`): the state a response leaves the
screen in, one value per code the program sets (COCRDUPC-044).

The screen derives from it which fields are enterable and which keys are shown
(COCRDUPC-045, COCRDUPC-046), and echoes it in `snapshot.state`. A value outside these seven
does not deserialise, which refuses the codes the program never sets (`X-COCRDUPC-8`).

CardUpdateView.description:
The 200 body of endpoint 9: the card as `3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS` shows it in state `S`, with
the snapshot the client echoes (COCRDUPC-002, COCRDUPC-016, COCRDUPC-017, COCRDUPC-044).

The card number is redacted and the card verification code absent (COCRDUPC-042, `E32`).
The screen shows the month and year of `expiration_date` in `EXPMON` and `EXPYEAR` and keeps
the day out of sight.

acct_id.description:
`ACCTSIDO`: the account as entered, or the list row's, 11 digits with their leading
zeros; never the card's own `CARD-ACCT-ID` (COCRDUPC-016, `X-COCRDUPC-2`).

card_num.description: `CARDSIDO`: the card number, twelve `*` followed by its last four digits (COCRDUPC-042).

card_ref.description: The card's `cards.card_ref` handle, which endpoint 10 takes in its path (COCRDUPC-043).

embossed_name.description:
`CRDNAMEO`: the stored name with `a` to `z` upper-cased and every other byte unchanged,
all 50 bytes, trailing spaces included (COCRDUPC-017).

expiration_date.description:
`CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE PIC X(10)` as a date, `null` when the stored date is blank
(COCRDUPC-017, CVACT02Y-005).

info_message.description:
`INFOMSGO` (40): `Details of selected card shown above`, the info line of state `S`
(COCRDUPC-016).

message.description:
`ERRMSGO`: always `null`, because a fetched card has no error message; every other
outcome is a `ScreenError` (COCRDUPC-002, COCRDUPC-016).

snapshot.description:
The fetched values in state `show_details`, echoed in every endpoint 10 request
(COCRDUPC-044).

status.description:
`CRDSTCDO` from `CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS PIC X(01)`: the stored byte, a space included
(COCRDUPC-017).

CardViewResponse.description:
The 200 body of endpoint 8: the found card as `1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS` shows it
(COCRDSLC-018 to COCRDSLC-023).

It holds no card verification code: the program moves the verification-code field of
`CVACT02Y` to no screen field (COCRDSLC-021).

acct_id.description:
`ACCTSIDO`: the account the request named, 11 digits with their leading zeros, never the
card's own account (COCRDSLC-014, COCRDSLC-018).

card_num.description:
`CARDSIDO`: the card number, all 16 digits for an administrator token and otherwise
twelve `*` followed by the last four digits (COCRDSLC-022, COCRDSLC-023).

card_ref.description:
The card's `cards.card_ref` handle, with which the screen reads the same card again while
the card input shows the returned number (COCRDSLC-018, COCRDSLC-026).

embossed_name.description:
`CRDNAMEO` from `CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME PIC X(50)`: its 50 stored bytes, trailing spaces
included (COCRDSLC-019).

expiration_date.description:
`CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE PIC X(10)` as a date, `null` when the stored date is blank
(COCRDSLC-019, CVACT02Y-005). The screen shows its month in `EXPMON` and its year in
`EXPYEAR` (COCRDSLC-024).

info_message.description:
`INFOMSGO` (40): the information message of a found card, `'   Displaying requested
details'` with its three leading spaces (COCRDSLC-020).

message.description:
`ERRMSGO`: always `null`, because a found card leaves `WS-RETURN-MSG` spaces; every other
outcome is a `ScreenError` (COCRDSLC-018).

status.description:
`CRDSTCDO` from `CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS PIC X(01)`: its stored byte, a space when it is a
space (COCRDSLC-019).

CoactupcAid.description:
The key of an endpoint 6 request.

`ENTER` runs the change check and the edits; `PF5` saves, and only when the echoed
`snapshot.state` is `N`. Any other key text is read as `ENTER`, as `0000-MAIN` processes
every other key, `PF12` included, as ENTER (COACTUPC-004); a value that is not a string is a
400.

CocrdupcAid.description:
The key of an endpoint 10 request.

`ENTER` runs the change check and the edits and asks for confirmation; `PF5` saves, and only
when the echoed `snapshot.state` is `changes_ok_not_confirmed`: in any other state it is
processed as `ENTER` (COCRDUPC-007). The screen submits every other key as `ENTER` and keeps
F3 and F12 to itself (COCRDUPC-008), so any other key name is a 400.

Cotrn02cAid.description:
The attention key of an endpoint 13 request, `TranAddRequest.aid` (COTRN02C-007).

`ENTER` and `PF5` are served. Any other key name is accepted, so that it gets the program's
own answer, 400 `Invalid key pressed. Please see below...` with nothing read or written, never
the rejection of an unreadable body (COTRN02C-006, COTRN02C-007). F3 and F4 are the screen's,
which serves them without a request (COTRN02C-004, COTRN02C-005).

CotrtlicAid.description:
The key of an endpoint 25 request. Every key without a label on the map is sent as ENTER
(COTRTLIC-014); F10 is always sent as `PF10`, and the domain decides whether it commits
(COTRTLIC-036).

CotrtupcAid.description:
The key of an endpoint 27 request (`EIBAID`): `ENTER`, `PF4` or `PF5` (COTRTUPC-043).

Any other key name the client sends is accepted, so that it gets the program's own answer,
400 `Invalid key pressed` with nothing read or written, never the rejection of an unreadable
body. F3 and F12 are the screen's, which serves them without a request (COTRTUPC-039 to
COTRTUPC-041, COTRTUPC-044).

FraudToggleResult.description:
The answer of F5, endpoint 23: `MARK-AUTH-FRAUD`, COPAUS2C's `AUTHFRDS` write and the
replace of the detail (COPAUS1C-028 to COPAUS1C-034).

After a commit, `message` is `AUTH MARKED FRAUD...` or `AUTH FRAUD REMOVED...` and `detail`
is the same authorization as replaced, its new fraud status and report date shown and its key
unchanged (COPAUS1C-032, COPAUS1C-034).

oneOf.description:
The authorization as replaced, after a commit; absent when the outcome carries no
detail.

message.description: The message row: the domain outcome's message (COPAUS1C-032, COPAUS1C-035).

MenuOptionDto.description:
One menu option: one row `BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS` fills, with what the screen needs to decide
ENTER on it (COMEN01C-013, COMEN01C-020, COMEN01C-021).

admin_only.description:
Whether the option is refused to a `U` user: the main menu's `'A'` user-type column,
which no shipped option has, and every admin-menu option, whose table has no user-type
column and which only an `A` token reaches (COMEN01C-020, COADM01C-012).

installed.description:
Whether the option's program can be taken, the outcome of the program's installation
check: `true` for every shipped option (COMEN01C-013, COADM01C-013).

number.description:
`CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NUM PIC 9(02)`: the option's two digits with the leading zero, `01` to
`11` on the main menu and `01` to `06` on the admin menu, the value the screen's
right-justified, zero-filled option input is matched against (COMEN01C-020).

program.description:
`CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME PIC X(08)` without trailing spaces, such as `COACTVWC`: the
program the option transfers to, whose route the client's program table gives
(COMEN01C-020).

text.description:
The row text as `BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS` strings it into the 40-byte `OPTNnnn` field
cleared to spaces: the two digits, `. `, the 35-byte name and one space, all 40 bytes,
trailing spaces included; for example `01. Account View` followed by 24 spaces
(COMEN01C-021, COADM01C-006 to COADM01C-011).

unavailable_message.description:
The text the screen shows when the option cannot be taken, as the program composes it,
or absent when the program composes none for the option. On the main menu only option
11 has one, its not-installed text; every admin-menu option carries
`This option is not installed ...`, which the admin screen also shows when a transfer
finds no screen (COMEN01C-015, COMEN01C-017, COADM01C-014).

MenuResponse.description:
The body of endpoints 2 and 3: the option table in table order and the program's rejection
texts (COMEN01C-004, COMEN01C-011, COMEN01C-020, COADM01C-005, COADM01C-014).

admin_only_message.description:
The text of an admin-only option refused to a `U` user,
`No access - Admin Only option... ` with its trailing space; absent on the admin menu,
which refuses no option by user type (COMEN01C-011, COADM01C-012).

invalid_option_message.description:
The text of an option the range edit refuses, `Please enter a valid option number...`,
as the program moves it (COMEN01C-011, COADM01C-014).

options.description:
The options in table order: 11 on the main menu, 6 on the admin menu (COMEN01C-020,
COADM01C-005).

user_type.description:
The caller's user type exactly as the verified token's `usr_type` claim holds it, the
value the main screen's admin-only check compares with `admin_only`; never taken from a
request field (AAP 0.5.1; COMEN01C-004). Absent on the admin menu, whose program compares
no user type (COADM01C-012).

example.invalid_option_message: Please enter a valid option number...

PageDirection.description:
The paging key of a collection request: `forward` (F8) or `backward` (F7). Absent, the
request is ENTER or a first entry.

ReportRequest.description:
The ten inputs of `CORPT0A` exactly as the screen sends them (CORPT00C-042). An absent
member is the empty text, which the program treats as blank.

Monthly and Yearly take their dates from the server's clock and ignore the date parts
(CORPT00C-007 to CORPT00C-010); Custom edits the six parts (CORPT00C-011 to CORPT00C-028).
The confirmation is read only once the report and its dates are set (CORPT00C-030 to
CORPT00C-033).

A member longer than its map field is a 400 naming it, with the field-length message
`FIELD_LENGTH_MESSAGE`. A date part holding a character other than a digit, unless every
character is a space, is a 400 naming it, with the digits-only message
`FIELD_NUMERIC_MESSAGE` (X-CORPT00C-5).

confirm.description:
`CONFIRM`, `PIC X(1)` (`CORPT00-038`): `Y` or `y` writes the job deck, `N` or `n` clears
the screen, blank asks for confirmation and any other character is rejected
(CORPT00C-030 to CORPT00C-033).

custom.description:
`CUSTOM`, `PIC X(1)` (`CORPT00-018`): selects the report of the date range below when
`monthly` and `yearly` are blank (CORPT00C-007).

end_day.description:
`EDTDD`, `PIC X(2)`, `NUM` (`CORPT00-032`): the end day of a custom report, digits or
blank (CORPT00C-015, CORPT00C-022).

end_month.description:
`EDTMM`, `PIC X(2)`, `NUM` (`CORPT00-030`): the end month of a custom report, digits or
blank (CORPT00C-014, CORPT00C-021).

end_year.description:
`EDTYYYY`, `PIC X(4)`, `NUM` (`CORPT00-034`): the end year of a custom report, digits or
blank (CORPT00C-016).

monthly.description:
`MONTHLY`, `PIC X(1)` (`CORPT00-012`): any character other than a space selects the
report of the current month (CORPT00C-007, CORPT00C-008).

start_day.description:
`SDTDD`, `PIC X(2)`, `NUM` (`CORPT00-024`): the start day of a custom report, digits or
blank (CORPT00C-012, CORPT00C-019).

start_month.description:
`SDTMM`, `PIC X(2)`, `NUM` (`CORPT00-022`): the start month of a custom report, digits
or blank (CORPT00C-011, CORPT00C-018).

start_year.description:
`SDTYYYY`, `PIC X(4)`, `NUM` (`CORPT00-026`): the start year of a custom report, digits
or blank (CORPT00C-013).

yearly.description:
`YEARLY`, `PIC X(1)` (`CORPT00-015`): selects the report of the current year when
`monthly` is blank (CORPT00C-007, CORPT00C-010).

ReportResult.description:
The 200 of endpoint 14: the message row and, when the job deck was written, its file name.

- Written deck: `message` is the report name and ` report submitted for printing ...`, such
  as `Monthly report submitted for printing ...`, and `job_deck` the generation file's name
  (CORPT00C-038).
- Confirmation `N` or `n`: an empty `message` and no `job_deck`; the screen empties every
  input (CORPT00C-032).

Every other outcome, the prompt of a blank confirmation included, is a `ScreenError` with the
status its CORPT00C row assigns (CORPT00C-029 to CORPT00C-033, CORPT00C-037).

job_deck.description:
The name of the generation file the deck was written to, such as `TRNRPT00.G0001`:
the file name alone, never a directory or an absolute path, so the response does not
disclose where the server keeps its files. Absent when no deck was written.

message.description: The message row as CORPT00C words it, without trailing spaces.

ScreenError.description:
The standard body of an error response: the message row of the screen and the request field
the program puts the cursor on, with the HTTP status the response carries. Endpoints 24 and 25
may answer a program error with their page instead.

Serialised as `{"message": …, "field": …}`, `field` omitted when absent. The status travels
as the response status only and is no part of the body or of the schema. A deserialised
value, as a test reads one back, has status 500, since the body does not carry it.

The schema name is `ScreenError`: the frontend's generated types refer to
`components["schemas"]["ScreenError"]` (Generated API Types Only).

field.description:
The request field the message names and the screen puts the cursor on, as its wire
name, such as `user_id` or `rows[3].description`.

message.description:
The message row, exactly as the program words it; it never holds a full card number,
SSN, card verification code or password.

ScreenResult.description:
The body of a 200 that carries only the message row: user add (endpoint 17, COUSR01C), user
update (endpoint 19, COUSR02C) and user delete (endpoint 20, COUSR03C).

message.description:
The message row exactly as the program words it, such as `User NEWUSR01 has been added
...` (COUSR01C-021), `User USER0001 has been updated ...` (COUSR02C-029) or
`User USER0001 has been deleted ...` (COUSR03C-019).

SignonRequest.description:
The sign-on request: the user ID and password typed on the sign-on screen.

Both members are optional on the wire and default to empty text. Each admits at most the 8
characters of its map field (COSGN00-027, COSGN00-031); a longer value is rejected with a 400
naming the field. The program's edits then reject a value whose 8 characters do not fit 8
bytes of printable ASCII, and answer a blank field with its own message.

password.description:
`PASSWDI PIC X(8)`, a dark field: the password as typed, at most 8 characters. Accepted,
never returned.

user_id.description:
`USERIDI PIC X(8)`: the user ID as typed, at most 8 characters. Upper-cased by the
program before the read, so `user0001` signs on as `USER0001` (COSGN00C-009).

SignonResponse.description:
A successful sign-on: the session token, the COMMAREA identity it carries and the screen
the program transfers to (COSGN00C-014 to COSGN00C-016).

next_route.description:
The route of the screen the program transfers to: `/admin` (COADM01C) for type `A`,
`/menu` (COMEN01C) for every other type (COSGN00C-015, COSGN00C-016).

token.description:
The HS256 bearer token for every other endpoint, with claims `sub` (the user ID),
`usr_type`, `iat` and `exp`.

user_id.description:
`CDEMO-USER-ID PIC X(08)`: the upper-cased user ID the user was read by, without its
trailing spaces (COSGN00C-014, COCOM01Y-005).

user_type.description:
`CDEMO-USER-TYPE PIC X(01)`: the stored user type, `A` for an administrator and `U` for
a user, as its single character unchanged (COSGN00C-014, COCOM01Y-006).

TranAddCopiedFields.description:
The data fields the screen shows with the confirmation prompt, each as its map field holds
it (COTRN02C-057).

The text fields keep their trailing spaces, the amount is COTRN02C's `+99999999.99` edit and
the dates are typed, `None` for a blank date; the screen writes each date into its input as
`YYYY-MM-DD`, the ten characters the COBOL shows.

amount.description: `TRNAMT`: a sign, eight digits, `.` and two digits (COTRN02C-036, COTRN02C-055).

TranAddFields.description:
The eleven data fields of `COTRN2A`, each the raw text of its map field and at most its map
`LENGTH`; an absent member is the empty text (COTRN02C-060).

The service hands them to COTRN02C's edits unchanged, the dates and the amount included.
On PF5 the program replaces them with the copied transaction's, whatever they hold
(COTRN02C-054).

amount.description:
`TRNAMT`, the amount as text in the hinted `-99999999.99` layout, which COTRN02C edits,
`LENGTH=12` (`COTRN02-033`).

cat_cd.description: `TCATCD`, the category code, four digits as typed, `LENGTH=4` (`COTRN02-024`).

orig_date.description:
`TORIGDT`, the original date as typed, `YYYY-MM-DD`, raw input to COTRN02C's date edit,
`LENGTH=10` (`COTRN02-036`).

proc_date.description:
`TPROCDT`, the processing date as typed, raw input to COTRN02C's date edit, `LENGTH=10`
(`COTRN02-039`).

acct_id.description:
`ACTIDIN`, the account key as typed, `LENGTH=11` (`COTRN02-013`). A non-blank account
decides the key, whatever `card_num` holds (COTRN02C-010, COTRN02C-011).

aid.description:
The attention key: `ENTER` or `PF5`. Any other key name is answered with 400 `Invalid key
pressed. Please see below...` and no field, before anything is read (COTRN02C-007).

card_num.description:
`CARDNIN`, the card key as typed, `LENGTH=16` (`COTRN02-017`); read only when `acct_id`
is blank (COTRN02C-015, COTRN02C-016). Write-only: it is request input and never part of
a response.

confirm.description:
`CONFIRM`, `Y`, `y`, `N`, `n` or blank as typed, `LENGTH=1` (`COTRN02-057`); any other
value is COTRN02C's own edit (COTRN02C-040 to COTRN02C-042).

TranAddResult.description:
The 200 body of endpoint 13: what the COBOL screen shows after the confirmation prompt or
after the add (COTRN02C-041, COTRN02C-049, COTRN02C-057).

- **Prompt** (confirmation blank, `N` or `n`): the account and the card, entered or filled
  in from the cross-reference, the card redacted; the data fields as edited, in `copied`;
  field `confirm`; message `Confirm to add this transaction...`; no `new_tran_id`. Nothing
  was written.
- **Added** (confirmation `Y` or `y`): every key and data field empty, field `acct_id`, the
  success message and the new transaction ID.

acct_id.description:
`ACTIDIN`: the 11 digits entered, or filled in from the cross-reference on the card path
(COTRN02C-017); absent after the add.

card_num.description:
`CARDNIN`: the card of the transaction, entered or filled in from the cross-reference on
the account path, as twelve `*` and its last four digits (COTRN02C-012, `E32`); absent
after the add.

oneOf.description:
The data fields the prompt shows: the request's on ENTER, the copied transaction's on
PF5, each as COTRN02C edited it; absent after the add (COTRN02C-056, COTRN02C-057).

field.description:
The request member the cursor goes to: `confirm` after the prompt, `acct_id` after the
add (COTRN02C-041, COTRN02C-049).

message.description:
The message row: `Confirm to add this transaction...`, or the success message with the
new ID (COTRN02C-041, COTRN02C-049).

new_tran_id.description: The 16-digit ID of the inserted transaction, only after the add (COTRN02C-049).

TranListEntryKey.description:
The key of the transfer that brought the screen up, sent with the first request only
(COTRN00C-003, COTRN00C-004, X-COTRN00C-2).

TranListQuery.description:
The query string of endpoint 11: the key sent, the search value and the echoed paging
state. Every member is optional; with none the request is an ENTER with a blank search over
the state a menu entry starts from (COTRN00C-002, COTRN00C-011).

oneOf.description: F8 (`forward`) or F7 (`backward`); absent for ENTER and for a first entry.

The transfer key of the first request after the screen is brought up; when present it
decides the request, and `direction` and `start_tran_id` are not read.

has_next_page.description:
`CDEMO-CT00-NEXT-PAGE-FLG`, echoed from the last response: `true` is `Y`; absent or
`false` is any other value.

page_no.description:
`CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM PIC 9(08)`, echoed from the last response; absent is 0. Page 0 is a
real state, after a first entry that showed no row or a rejected search (COTRN00C-004,
COTRN00C-013), so 0 is admitted.

page_size.description:
Rows of a page, 1 to 100, default 10, the rows of `COTRN0A` (Bounded Pagination); 422
outside that range. The screen never sends it.

start_tran_id.description:
`TRNIDIN`, the search value as typed, at most the 16 characters of the map field
(COTRN00-015). Blank starts at the lowest ID; anything else but 16 digits is answered 400
`Tran ID must be Numeric ...` by the program's own edit (COTRN00C-011 to COTRN00C-013).
Read on ENTER only.

TranListResponse.description:
The 200 of endpoint 11: the rows, the paging state the screen echoes with its next request
and the message the program moved last (COTRN00C-035).

message.description:
The message row, `null` when the program moved none, such as `You have reached the
bottom of the page...` (COTRN00C-017) or `You are already at the top of the page...`
(COTRN00C-022).

page_no.description:
`CDEMO-CT00-PAGE-NUM PIC 9(08)`: echo it as `page_no`. The screen shows it as eight
digits with leading zeros, and only after a page was read (COTRN00C-036).

rows.description:
The page read: exactly `page_size` slots, row 1 first, `null` for a blank row. Empty
when `rows_kept` is true.

rows_kept.description:
True when nothing was read: F7 at the top or F8 at the bottom, where the screen keeps
the rows, page number, search value and selectors it shows (COTRN00C-021,
COTRN00C-022).

example.message: You have reached the bottom of the page...

TranListRow.description:
One list row of `COTRN0A`, rows 1 to 10 at screen lines 10 to 19 (COTRN00C-028 to
COTRN00C-034).

description.description: `TDESCnn`: the first 26 bytes of `TRAN-DESC`, trailing spaces included (COTRN00C-031).

display_date.description:
`TDATEnn`: the `MM/DD/YY` date the screen shows, built by the program's rule from
`orig_ts`, so the screen formats nothing; `null` for a blank `TRAN-ORIG-TS`, whose COBOL
display no source fixes (COTRN00C-029, COTRN00C-030).

orig_ts.description:
`TRAN-ORIG-TS` as its typed timestamp, `null` when the field is blank (COTRN00C-029;
Typed Dates and Timestamps).

tran_id.description:
`TRNIDnn`: the stored `TRAN-ID`, all 16 bytes as stored, which the `S` selection carries
to COTRN01 (COTRN00C-028).

TranTypeActionRequest.description:
The body of endpoint 27: the key, and the description `TRTYDSCI PIC X(50)` as typed.

The description is the raw map input: COTRTUPC stores it and owns its edits, the required
and alphanumeric tests and their messages (COTRTUPC-004, COTRTUPC-018, COTRTUPC-019). Only
the map `LENGTH` is checked here, the server half of `COTRTUP-016`; a longer value is a 400
naming `description`. Absent, it is the empty text, as the domain reads an absent field.

description.description: `TRTYDSCI PIC X(50)`, as typed: up to 50 characters.

TranTypeActionResult.description:
The 200 of endpoint 27: the screen the step sends, and whether it wrote.

ENTER with a valid change gives state `changes_ok_not_confirmed` and info row
`Changes validated.Press F5 to save`, nothing written (COTRTUPC-020). PF5 gives state
`changes_okayed_and_done`, info row `Changes committed to database`, after the update or the
insert that follows an update finding no row (COTRTUPC-024, COTRTUPC-026). PF4 gives state
`delete_done`, info row `Delete successful.` (COTRTUPC-032).

committed.description:
Whether the step wrote to `db2.transaction_type` and the service committed it: a save or
a delete. The info row alone does not tell: a failed save also leaves state
`changes_okayed_and_done` (COTRTUPC-027, COTRTUPC-028).

deleted.description: Whether the committed write was the delete of the type shown (COTRTUPC-032).

description.description:
`TRTYDSCO PIC X(50)`: the description validated or saved, the `FUNCTION TRIM` of the
typed text padded to 50 characters, which is also the value stored (COTRTUPC-020,
COTRTUPC-023). Absent after a delete, whose screen keeps the fetched values the screen
already holds (COTRTUPC-030), and on the fresh screen.

info_message.description: The info row, `WS-INFO-MSG`, for the state the screen enters (COTRTUPC-045).

message.description: The error row, `WS-RETURN-MSG`, exactly as the program words it; absent when empty.

state.description: The state the screen enters, which it holds until the next request.

type_code.description: `TRTYPCDO PIC X(2)`, the code shown without trailing spaces; empty on the fresh screen.

TranTypeListActionRequest.description: The body of endpoint 25: the key, the map input and the echoed state.

page_size.description:
Rows per page, 1 to 100, 7 when absent; a page never holds more than the seven
positions of the map. Outside 1 to 100 the request is rejected with 422 (Bounded
Pagination).

rows.description:
The seven rows, top to bottom; missing rows are blank. More than seven do not
deserialise, since the map has no field for them.

state.description: The `state` of the previous response, echoed unchanged.

type_filter.description:
`TRTYPEI PIC X(2)`, as typed: the domain's type-filter edit owns its message
(COTRTLIC-027, COTRTLIC-028).

TranTypeListActionResult.description:
The response of endpoint 25: the page as re-read, or the state's rows where nothing was
read, with the row errors, the messages, the commit and the new state.

Answer with the value itself: its `IntoResponse` sends the audited status of the outcome,
200, 400, 404 or 500 (COTRTLIC.md, "Reading the table"), with this body.

has_next_page.description: Whether a next page exists for the page shown.

info_message.description:
The info line, `INFOMSG`: the confirmation prompt, the commit text or `Type U to
update, D to delete any record`.

message.description:
The error line, `ERRMSG`: an error, `No change detected with respect to database
values.` or the fixed start of a Db2 message (COTRTLIC-054; the rest is `HALTED(H3)`).

page_key.description: The new state as the opaque key the screen echoes with F7 and F8.

row_errors.description: The row fields in error, top to bottom.

rows.description: The seven positions shown, top to bottom; `null` is an empty position.

state.description:
The new state, the pending action set when ENTER validated one; the screen echoes it
with ENTER and F10.

TranTypeListFilterStatus.description:
Whether a filter of the response adds a predicate, and whether it is in error, red with the
focus (COTRTLIC-028, COTRTLIC-031, COTRTLIC-057).

TranTypeListPendingAction.description:
The pending flags of the state, `WS-CA-DELETE-FLAG` and `WS-CA-UPDATE-FLAG`, which can be
set together (COTRTLIC-043).

TranTypeListQuery.description:
The query of endpoint 24: the screen load, and F7 or F8 under the filters on the screen.

With both `page_key` and `direction` it is F7 or F8 from the state `page_key` encodes,
with the filter edits run on `type_filter` and `desc_filter` as on ENTER, so a changed filter
moves to page 1 of it (COTRTLIC-007 to COTRTLIC-013, X-COTRTLIC-6). Without either it is the
screen load, a first entry that ignores every other member (COTRTLIC-002).

desc_filter.description: The description filter on the screen, `TRDESCI PIC X(50)`, as typed.

oneOf.description: `forward` for F8, `backward` for F7; absent, the request is the screen load.

page_key.description:
The `page_key` of the previous response, echoed unchanged; the screen never builds one.
Absent or empty, the request is the screen load.

page_size.description:
Rows per page, 1 to 100, 7 when absent; a page never holds more than the seven
positions of the map. Outside 1 to 100 the request is rejected with 422 (Bounded
Pagination).

type_filter.description:
The type filter on the screen when F7 or F8 is pressed, `TRTYPEI PIC X(2)`, as typed:
the domain's type-filter edit owns its message.

TranTypeListResponse.description:
The response of endpoint 24: the page shown and the state the next request echoes.

Answer with the value itself: its `IntoResponse` sends the audited status of the outcome,
200, 400 for a filter in error or 500 for a store failure, with this body.

has_next_page.description: Whether a next page exists for the page shown.

info_message.description:
The info line, `INFOMSG`, up to 45 characters, such as `Type U to update, D to delete
any record`.

message.description:
The error line, `ERRMSG`: an error, or a paging message such as `No more pages to
display`.

page_key.description: The state as the opaque key the screen echoes with F7 and F8.

rows.description: The seven positions of the page, top to bottom; `null` is an empty position.

state.description: The state, which the screen echoes with ENTER and F10.

TranTypeListRow.description:
One row of the state: a type code and its description, either as the last read returned
them (`WS-CA-EACH-ROW-OUT`, the description as stored) or as the previous response showed
them (`TRTTYPn`, `TRTYPDn`, without trailing spaces).

type_code.description: The two-character type code, `WS-CA-ROW-TR-CODE-OUT PIC X(02)`; empty for a blank code.

TranTypeListRowError.description:
A field of one row that the response flags in error, red with the focus (COTRTLIC-021,
COTRTLIC-022, COTRTLIC-025, COTRTLIC-026).

message.description:
The error line's message, the one message COTRTLIC sends with the flagged fields
(COTRTLIC-033).

TranTypeListRowInput.description:
One row of an endpoint 25 request: the selection and the description as typed.

The type code is no input: the 3270 returns the protected code field as displayed, so the
codes are the state's (COTRTLIC-017).

description.description:
`TRTYPDn PIC X(50)`: read only at the row the previous response left enterable
(COTRTLIC-018).

selection.description:
`TRTSELn PIC X(1)`: `U` update, `D` delete, blank for none. Codes are case-sensitive,
and any other value is the domain's invalid action code (COTRTLIC-021).

TranTypeListSelectors.description: Whether the previous response left the selectors enterable (COTRTLIC-018).

text.description:
The text shown, without trailing spaces: as received while a selection is non-blank or
the filter is valid or in error, empty otherwise and on the screen load.

TranTypeListShownRow.description:
One row of a response as `2200-SETUP-ARRAY-ATTRIBS` and `2300-SCREEN-ARRAY-INIT` show it
(COTRTLIC-056).

description.description:
The description, `TRTYPDO`, without trailing spaces: as read, or on the row of a single
`U` the description received, `*` when blank (COTRTLIC-040, COTRTLIC-041).

description_enterable.description:
Whether the description is enterable for the next request: only on the row of a single
`U` whose update has not completed. A description in error is enterable and has a row
error.

highlighted.description: Whether the row is the one a single `D` or `U` highlights, in the neutral colour.

selection.description: The selection, `TRTSELO`: as typed, empty when blank, after a commit or a page move.

selector_enterable.description:
Whether the selector is enterable for the next request; a selector in error is
enterable and has a row error.

TranTypeListState.description:
The list state: COTRTLIC's COMMAREA and what the previous response left on the screen.

The server returns it with every response of endpoints 24 and 25, and the screen sends it
back unchanged with every ENTER and F10. It carries no authority: the domain rebuilds it
through its total constructor, re-runs every edit and re-reads the row of every commit.

desc_filter.description: `WS-CA-TYPE-DESC PIC X(50)`: the description filter of the displayed page, as typed.

description_entry.description:
The screen row, 1 to 7, whose description the previous response left enterable: the row
of a single `U` whose update has not completed (COTRTLIC-040).

first_key.description:
`WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE PIC X(02)`, from which the displayed page is re-read; absent when
blank.

last_key.description: `WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE PIC X(02)`, from which F8 reads the next page; absent when blank.

last_page_shown.description:
`WS-CA-LAST-PAGE-DISPLAYED`: whether an F8 already ended on the last page
(COTRTLIC-008, COTRTLIC-009).

next_page_exists.description: `WS-CA-NEXT-PAGE-IND`: whether the forward read found a row after the page.

page_no.description:
`WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM PIC 9(1)`: 1 to 9, or 0 after a filter change that no read has
followed yet (COTRTLIC-013, COTRTLIC-029).

rows.description:
The seven rows as the last read returned them, top to bottom; `null` is a position the
read left empty (COTRTLIC-004, COTRTLIC-012).

screen_rows.description:
The seven rows the previous response showed, top to bottom; `null` is a position it
left empty. The 3270 returns these protected fields as displayed (COTRTLIC-017,
COTRTLIC-018).

selected_row.description:
`WS-CA-ROW-SELECTED`: the screen row, 1 to 7, of the last accepted selection; absent for
none (COTRTLIC-023).

selectors.description: Whether the previous response left the selectors enterable.

type_filter.description: `WS-CA-TYPE-CD PIC X(02)`: the type filter of the displayed page, as typed.

TranTypeMaintState.description:
`TTUP-CHANGE-ACTION PIC X(1)` (`COTRTUPC.cbl:296-327`): the state a response leaves the
screen in, one value per value the program's 88-levels name.

The screen keeps it until the next request and derives from it the keys it shows, the fields
it protects and, after an error response, the info row (COTRTUPC-045, COTRTUPC-046). It carries
no authority, and no request sends it.

TranTypeView.description:
The 200 of endpoint 26, the fetch: the screen ENTER sends in the fresh or X state.

A row found gives state `show_details` with the stored code and description and the search
prompt as info row (COTRTUPC-009). A code no row holds gives state `details_not_found` with
the normalised code, no description, error row `No record found for this key in database`
and info row `Press F05 to add. F12 to cancel` (COTRTUPC-010).

description.description:
`TRTYDSCO PIC X(50)`: the stored description up to its stored length, trailing spaces
kept, since a value saved through COTRTUPC is stored padded to 50 (COTRTUPC-009,
COTRTUPC-023). Absent when no row holds the code.

info_message.description:
The info row, `WS-INFO-MSG`, for the state the screen enters (COTRTUPC-045); the screen
centres it in `INFOMSG`.

message.description: The error row, `WS-RETURN-MSG`, exactly as the program words it; absent when empty.

state.description: The state the screen enters, which it holds until the next request.

type_code.description:
`TRTYPCDO PIC X(2)`, the code shown without trailing spaces: the stored code of a row
found, or the normalised key of a code no row holds (COTRTUPC-008). The screen sends it
back as `{type_code}` of endpoint 27.

example.info_message: Enter transaction type to be maintained

TranViewResponse.description:
The transaction as the `COTRN1A` map shows it after a successful read: the 200 body of
endpoint 12 (COTRN01C-015 to COTRN01C-028).

The body is the same for a `U` and an `A` token, because COTRN01C checks no user type
(COTRN01C-015). It has no `Deserialize`: it holds a [`CardNumber`], which no request may
carry back.

amount.description:
`TRNAMT PIC X(12)`, from `TRAN-AMT PIC S9(09)V99` through `WS-TRAN-AMT PIC +99999999.99`:
`+00000050.47`, `-00000012.00`, and `+23456789.01` for 123456789.01, whose ninth integer
digit the picture has no position for (COTRN01C-022, X-COTRN01C-1).

card_num.description:
`CARDNUM`, from `TRAN-CARD-NUM PIC X(16)`: twelve `*` and the last four characters of the
stored field, never the full value; the COBOL moves all 16 bytes (COTRN01C-017, E32).

cat_cd.description:
`TCATCD PIC X(4)`, from `TRAN-CAT-CD PIC 9(04)`: the four digits with their leading
zeros, category 5 as `0005` (COTRN01C-019).

description.description: `TDESC PIC X(60)`, from `TRAN-DESC PIC X(100)`: its first 60 bytes (COTRN01C-021).

merchant_city.description:
`MCITY PIC X(25)`, from `TRAN-MERCHANT-CITY PIC X(50)`: its first 25 bytes
(COTRN01C-027).

merchant_id.description:
`MID PIC X(9)`, from `TRAN-MERCHANT-ID PIC 9(09)`: the nine digits with their leading
zeros (COTRN01C-025).

merchant_name.description:
`MNAME PIC X(30)`, from `TRAN-MERCHANT-NAME PIC X(50)`: its first 30 bytes
(COTRN01C-026).

merchant_zip.description: `MZIP`, from `TRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP PIC X(10)`: the 10 bytes as stored (COTRN01C-028).

message.description:
`ERRMSG`, the message row: always `null`, because every pass clears `WS-MESSAGE` and a
successful read moves no message into it (COTRN01C-015).

orig_ts.description:
`TORIGDT`, from `TRAN-ORIG-TS PIC X(26)`: the typed timestamp in whichever layout it was
stored, `null` when the field is blank. The screen shows its date part, the ten bytes the
COBOL moves (COTRN01C-023).

proc_ts.description:
`TPROCDT`, from `TRAN-PROC-TS PIC X(26)`: as `orig_ts`; a transaction posted by
`posttran` carries its posting instant (COTRN01C-024).

source.description: `TRNSRC`, from `TRAN-SOURCE PIC X(10)`: the 10 bytes as stored (COTRN01C-020).

tran_id.description: `TRNID`, from `TRAN-ID PIC X(16)`: the record's 16-byte key as stored (COTRN01C-016).

type_cd.description: `TTYPCD`, from `TRAN-TYPE-CD PIC X(02)`: the 2 bytes as stored (COTRN01C-018).

UserAddRequest.description:
The body of endpoint 17: the five input fields of `COUSR1A`, each the raw text of its map
field (COUSR01C-006).

Every member is optional on the wire and empty when absent. `Debug` prints `********` in
place of the password, which is never serialised (Cardholder Data Redaction).

first_name.description:
`FNAME`, `PIC X(20)`: the first name, as typed, at most 20 bytes of printable ASCII
(`0x20`–`0x7E`; COUSR01-013).

last_name.description:
`LNAME`, `PIC X(20)`: the last name, as typed, at most 20 bytes of printable ASCII
(`0x20`–`0x7E`; COUSR01-016).

password.description:
`PASSWD`, `PIC X(8)`, a dark field: the new user's password, stored as typed and hashed,
at most 8 bytes of printable ASCII (`0x20`–`0x7E`; COUSR01-022, COUSR01C-018).
Write-only: never sent back.

user_id.description:
`USERID`, `PIC X(8)`: the ID of the user to add, as typed and compared byte for byte
with the stored IDs, at most 8 bytes of printable ASCII (`0x20`–`0x7E`; COUSR01-019,
COUSR01C-023).

user_type.description:
`USRTYPE`, `PIC X(1)`: `A` for an administrator, any other non-blank character of
printable ASCII (`0x20`–`0x7E`) for a regular user (COUSR01-025, COUSR01C-015).

UserListQuery.description:
The query string of endpoint 16: the search field, the paging key and direction, the paging
state the last response returned, and the page size.

No member is required: a request without any is the first entry of the screen, ENTER with a
blank search field (COUSR00C-003, COUSR00C-012).

oneOf.description: `forward` for F8, `backward` for F7; absent for ENTER and the first entry.

has_next_page.description:
`has_next_page` of the last response, echoed: `CDEMO-CU00-NEXT-PAGE-FLG`. F8 without it,
or with `false`, answers `You are already at the bottom of the page...` and reads nothing
(COUSR00C-020).

page_key.description:
The user ID F7 or F8 reads from: the first user ID shown for `backward`, the last for
`forward` (COUSR00C-017, COUSR00C-022). Takes the place of `first_key` or `last_key`
respectively; ignored without a `direction`.

page_no.description:
`page_no` of the last response, echoed: `CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM PIC 9(08)`, so 0 to
99999999 (COUSR00C-006). Absent, page 0, the page number of a first entry. F7 reads only
above page 1 (COUSR00C-021, COUSR00C-022).

page_size.description:
Rows per page, 1 to 100; absent, the map's 10 (Bounded Pagination). Outside the range,
422. The screen never sends it.

start_user_id.description:
`USRIDIN`, the search field: ENTER lists from the first user ID at or above it, as typed,
with no edit; absent or blank, from the first user (COUSR00C-012). F7 and F8 ignore it
(COUSR00C-017). At most the map's 8 characters (COUSR00-015).

UserListResponse.description:
The 200 of endpoint 16, a page or a message with the paging state (COUSR00C-006,
COUSR00C-013 to COUSR00C-025).

The `ScreenError`s are the handler's: 401 and 403 from the gate, 400 for a member that
breaks its rule, 422 for `page_size`, and 500 `Unable to lookup User...` (COUSR00C-026).

first_key.description:
`CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST`, the key of F7: the user ID of row 1 when this page filled it,
otherwise the key the request carried; `null` when blank (COUSR00C-016). Echo it as the
next request's `first_key`, and as its `page_key` for `backward`.

has_next_page.description:
`CDEMO-CU00-NEXT-PAGE-FLG` = `Y`: whether F8 reads (COUSR00C-014, COUSR00C-020). F7 sets
it whether or not a user follows (COUSR00C-021). Echo it as the next request's
`has_next_page`.

last_key.description:
`CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST`, the key of F8: the user ID of the last row when this page filled
it, otherwise the key the request carried; `null` when blank (COUSR00C-016). Echo it as
the next request's `last_key`, and as its `page_key` for `forward`.

message.description:
The message row: `You have reached the bottom of the page...`, `You have reached the top
of the page...`, `You are already at the bottom of the page...`, `You are already at the
top of the page...` or `You are at the top of the page...`; `null` for none
(COUSR00C-014 to COUSR00C-025).

page_no.description:
`CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM PIC 9(08)`; the screen shows it as eight digits with leading zeros
(COUSR00C-029). Echo it as the next request's `page_no`.

rows.description:
The page: `page_size` row positions, row 1 first, `null` for a blank row (COUSR00C-013,
COUSR00C-018, COUSR00C-024). `null` when nothing was read: the screen keeps the rows, page
number and search field it shows (COUSR00C-020, COUSR00C-021).

UserListRow.description:
One row of the list: the four `SEC-USER-DATA` fields `POPULATE-USER-DATA` moves to the map,
trailing spaces removed (COUSR00C-028).

There is no password member: `SEC-USR-PWD` never reaches the map, and the list never reads
the stored hash (CSUSR01Y-004, Cardholder Data Redaction).

user_id.description:
`USRIDnn` (8), `SEC-USR-ID`: the user ID a `U` or `D` selection carries to the update or
delete screen (COUSR00C-008, COUSR00C-009).

user_type.description:
`UTYPEnn` (1), `SEC-USR-TYPE`: `A` for an administrator, `U` for a regular user, as
stored.

UserUpdateRequest.description:
The body of endpoint 19: the four input fields of the update map, each the raw text of its
map field (`FNAME`, `LNAME`, `PASSWD`, `USRTYPE`).

Each field is validated against its map `LENGTH`, the server half of its `both` row of
`modern/audit/screens.md`: `first_name` and `last_name` 20 (COUSR02-017, COUSR02-020),
`password` 8 (COUSR02-023) and `user_type` 1 (COUSR02-026), and against the `PIC X(n)`
field it is stored in: at most that many bytes, each printable ASCII (`0x20`–`0x7E`), or
`LOW-VALUES`, the field's width in NUL bytes. A value that fails either is a 400 naming the
field, before any program edit, so a password is stored with exactly the bytes sent.

A name or type that is absent is the empty text, and an empty, all-space or `LOW-VALUES`
value passes both rules, so the program's own blank-field edits answer it with their
messages, in its order (COUSR02C-019 to COUSR02C-022); no value edit applies to the type
(COUSR02C-023).

The password is optional and write-only: omitted or `null`, the stored hash is kept (`E27`).
It never leaves through `Serialize`, so a client that sends one writes the JSON itself, and
`Debug` shows a supplied one as `********`.

first_name.description: `FNAME`, `PIC X(20)`: at most 20 bytes of printable ASCII (`0x20`–`0x7E`).

last_name.description: `LNAME`, `PIC X(20)`: at most 20 bytes of printable ASCII (`0x20`–`0x7E`).

password.description:
`PASSWD`, `PIC X(8)`, dark on the map: the new password, at most 8 bytes of printable
ASCII (`0x20`–`0x7E`), or absent to keep the stored one. Never returned by any endpoint.

user_type.description:
`USRTYPE`, `PIC X(1)`: the type to store for the target user, one byte of printable
ASCII (`0x20`–`0x7E`).

UserView.description:
The answer of endpoint 18 for a user that has a row: the row's ID, names and type, and the
prompt each of the two sharing programs sends after its read (COUSR02C-012, COUSR02C-014,
COUSR03C-011, COUSR03C-012).

Each stored value is shown without its trailing spaces, the trimmed view of `PicX`, as the
map field displays it. No password is carried (`E27`).

delete_prompt.description:
COUSR03C's read prompt, `Press PF5 key to delete this user ...`, which the delete screen
shows in the message row (COUSR03C-012).

update_prompt.description:
COUSR02C's read prompt, `Press PF5 key to save your updates ...`, which the update screen
shows in the message row (COUSR02C-014).

user_id.description: `SEC-USR-ID PIC X(08)`, the key the user was read by.

user_type.description:
`SEC-USR-TYPE PIC X(01)`: `A` for an admin, `U` for a user, or any other character
COUSR01C or COUSR02C stored as typed.
